claims.claim: Heiner García of NorthScan co-authored published investigations with ANY.RUN and BCA LTD on DPRK IT workers.
claims.method: Both ANY.RUN posts name Heiner García from NorthScan and Mauro Eldritch from BCA LTD as collaborators, and part 2 states it was written by Mauro and Heiner.

claims.claim: A SEAL Intel report by Heiner covers the shift of DPRK IT workers to recruiters.
claims.method: The Radar page is dated Nov 07, 2025, credits SEAL Intel and Heiner Garcia, and describes Heiner as a SEAL Intel member.

claims.claim: Heiner presented this research at Insomni'hack and DEF CON.
claims.method: The NorthScan About page states both presentations. The Insomni'hack talk page loaded but the fetched text did not name the speaker, and no DEF CON page was found.

claims.claim: A working private platform stores and connects GitHub accounts, takes profile snapshots and maps follower networks.
claims.method: The platform is private by the applicant's own statement, so it cannot be inspected publicly. A supervised walkthrough is offered to curators only.

claims.claim: More than two years of direct research into DPRK IT worker operations underlies the platform.
claims.method: The site and linked articles show published research, with the NorthScan footer dated 2025. The duration claim was not independently confirmed.

claims.claim: NorthScan has no other committed funding and previously received about USD 2,000 from Giveth and TheDAO Security Fund.
claims.method: The Round 1 record exists. Round 1 amounts are tracked elsewhere. The statement about no other funding cannot be checked publicly.
